newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks close off a hair on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks close off a hair on profit-taking.

text.p: Mexican stocks reversed early gains to end lower Wednesday.

"What we saw today was just light profit-taking, which was to be expected after yesterday's speculative gains ahead of falls in primary rates," said Roberto Galvan, analyst at the Bursametrica consultancy.
The blue-chip IPC index fell 2.61 points to 3,268.84. Volume was regular at 71.6 million shares traded.
Banco de Mexico assigned bellwether 28-day Cetes (Treasury bond) rates at 29.08 percent at Tuesday night's primary auction, 0.77 percentage point down from last week.
Galvan said the market continued to be sluggish due to investors preferring to invest in New York and waiting for the peso to weaken and magnify peso returns.
On the broad market, 110 stocks were traded in all. Losers outnumbered winners 46 to 37.
Notable gainers in volume terms were auto parts maker Iasasa and mining firm Grupo Mexico.
Traders said Iasasa stock gained -- closing up 4 centavos (1 cent) at 37 centavos (5 cents) -- on bargain hunting after a debt restructuring plan for the firm had been announced Tuesday.
"GMexico traded strongly, and was in great demand, probably due to its involvement in railroad privatisation bidding," said a trader. GMexico ended up 1.25 pesos (13 cents) at 26.05 pesos ($3.30).

Publishers GFesa, followed by construction company Tribasa, headed the losers list. They ended down 9 centavos (1 cent) and 60 centavos (6 cents), respectively, at 1.66 pesos (21 cents) and 20.10 pesos ($2.55).
Traders said these two companies had a gloomy year-end outlook.
Dealers said they expected a very quiet session Thursday, because U.S. markets will be closed for Thanksgiving.
The Mexican stock market will be open Thursday but there will be no open outcry.
